title: Project C — Secure Full-Stack Application
summary: Build a small full-stack application (Vue frontend + Express or Rust backend) with security designed in: threat model first, then auth, authorization, input validation, and hardened headers — documented as you go.
requirements: A written threat model BEFORE implementation: assets, trust boundaries, top-5 threats with mitigations
Authentication: argon2/bcrypt password hashing, HttpOnly SameSite session cookies (or short-JWT + rotation)
Server-side authorization on every route: RBAC with at least two roles, ownership checks (no IDOR)
Input validation at the boundary with a schema; output encoding context-correct (no raw HTML injection)
SQL access fully parameterized (no string-built queries)
Security headers (helmet or equivalent), CORS allowlist, rate limiting on auth routes
Secrets from environment; zero secrets in code, repo, or logs
Security events logged (auth failures, role changes) without logging secrets
A security notes document: threat model, decisions, and residual risks

starterFiles.name: threat-model.md
starterFiles.code:
# Threat model — notes app

## Assets
- user credentials (password hashes)
- note contents (per-user private)
- session tokens

## Trust boundaries
- browser <-> API (untrusted input)
- API <-> database (parameterized access only)

## Top threats & mitigations
1. credential stuffing  -> rate limit /auth, argon2 hashing
2. XSS stealing sessions -> output encoding + CSP + HttpOnly cookies
3. IDOR on /notes/:id   -> ownership check server-side
4. SQL injection        -> parameterized queries only
5. secret leakage       -> env-only secrets, no secret logging

hints: Write the threat model FIRST and let it drive the milestone order — defense follows the model, not the other way around.
The IDOR test is simple: log in as user A and request user B's note id — the API must answer 404/403, not leak.
Rate limit /auth before you write the login handler; retrofitting limits is how they get forgotten.
completionCriteria: Threat model document exists and maps every mitigation to a threat
All authorization enforced server-side (ownership test passes)
Security events logged; headers and rate limits verified
